description.value:
You believe, as the Choir of Ash believes, that Uriel's Turning was corruption-forced tragedy rather than evil intent — and that it was also unfinished mercy the world still owes itself. Your Ward is not usually a person: it is the Kindling, a specific act of hastening-the-end that the Choir has entrusted to you — a wildfire left to burn, a dying reactor left uncapped, a soul marked for release rather than salvage. You protect the ending from being stopped.

The Answer

Triggers when someone tries to extinguish, salvage, or "mercifully" interrupt your Kindling — including an ally trying to save someone you've marked. You intervene against the interloper, not the fire.

Design note: this triggers against allies as readily as enemies. It's meant to create real friction at the table — use it deliberately.

Vows (spend Cinders)

Two Vows per Oath — full crunch in What You Learned. Further Vows are picked up as Sworn feats.

  • Kindling's Mark — touch a target judged worth hastening toward its end; your Strikes and Vows hit it harder for the encounter.
  • Ash Already Falling — you and nearby allies gain fire resistance scaling with your level for a minute.

cinderfall.incomplete: Real pf2e's own subclass-choice cards do auto-grant their signature reaction via a static GrantItem -- confirmed via pf2e-source/packs/pf2e/class-features/liberation.json (Champion's Cause card grants 'Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Liberating Step' directly, off the same ChoiceSet+GrantItem parent as this corpus's own sworn.oath.json). But tools/foundry/build_pack.py's resolve_grants() (line 368) only rewrites system.items slot entries into real UUIDs, and resolve_ancestry() (line 431) only resolves system.ancestry.slug on heritage cards -- there is no resolver for a literal GrantItem inside a feat's own system.rules pointing at a sibling card by slug. Every existing GrantItem in site/data/cards/feats/class/** uses only the dynamic {item|flags.system.rulesSelections.<flag>} form Foundry resolves at runtime from a ChoiceSet, never a static literal UUID pointing at another Cinderfall card -- shipping a hand-written Compendium string here would be a fabricated, unconfirmed value. This is a build-tooling gap, not specific to this card, and blocks the same pattern for every other class with an Oath/Path/Cause-style subclass.
